A checklist has been developed for terminal cleaning and decontamination of Ebola care facilities. This checklist outlines the necessary steps for waste management, cleaning, and decontamination processes. It also identifies the agencies and personnel required for facility inspection before, during, and after terminal cleaning. These include representatives from the Ministry of Health or relevant authorities, project officers, infection prevention and control (IPC) officers, cleaners, water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) officers, occupational health and safety officers (if available), laundry staff (optional), waste handlers, and security guards. The facility must not be reopened for other purposes until the cleaning and decontamination process is safely completed and documented using the checklist. For psychological reasons, it is recommended to repaint walls and refresh furniture if possible. Spraying rooms with disinfectants is not advised, as it is potentially hazardous, lacks proven disease control benefits, and may not reach all surfaces. However, spraying may be acceptable outdoors when it is the only feasible option or necessary for disinfecting sand or gravel floors. If spraying is used, it must be preceded by cleaning with water and detergent to remove contaminants and organic matter. Cleaners performing spraying must wear full personal protective equipment (PPE). The checklist includes specific recommendations for terminal cleaning and decontamination of Ebola care facilities. Cleaners, hygienists, and other personnel working in high-risk zones (red zones) must wear full PPE for all activities conducted before or during terminal cleaning. All intact objects and equipment suitable for cleaning and decontamination should be identified and labeled. Clean areas should be equipped with a full-length mirror, posters detailing PPE donning and removal steps, hand hygiene stations, and adequate stocks of necessary equipment. Decontamination areas should also include waste bins and equipment for proper cleaning. Environmental surfaces, including furniture, walls, and doors, must be thoroughly cleaned. Spills of blood, body fluids, secretions, or excretions should be covered with a rag or paper towel, wiped up, and disposed of in a designated infectious waste bucket or laundry container. Disinfectants, such as a solution containing 5000 ppm available free chlorine, should be used for cleaning. Dust-holding rags must not be shaken out to prevent contamination. Additional considerations include desludging septic tanks if necessary, ensuring proper transportation of oversized or heavy materials, and conducting sanitary surveys of water points used by the Ebola treatment center. If the site is dismantled, pipes must be removed to an approved dumping site. This checklist serves as a tool for the intended users and is not designed for data collection by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The information collected is solely for the purpose of ensuring safe and effective terminal cleaning and decontamination of Ebola care facilities.
